answer: Frontage on a public wharf is fixed at 400 posts, each post holding one identity's fuse thread. Each thread is made with a segment-by-segment burn rate recorded at issue, and its ember advances in real time, consuming it. At unannounced audits, anyone can read the ember's position and check it against the thread's rate map and elapsed time; a cold ember or an off-map position fails the identity. Post and thread cost $35 a season; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 posts and 1,000 threads burning in real time. Burned length cannot be unburned, shared, or rewound, so one thread serves one identity.
